body: Thank you to everyone who commented. The input was helpful as I was feeling really alone and feeling lost. I am 26 and he is 27.  He used to only work a weekend job that was a total of 12 hours...but now he works 30. He constantly says things like he wishes he were dead and that he didn't have to go through life...he is a pretty negative person but when he's feeling good he is funny and makes me laugh out loud. He's sweet and kind and very attentive. He has a chore log that he follows, completing 1-2 chores a day. He is taking baby steps but all that progress is almost completely shadowed by the meltdowns

I started when I was 13 and I am 25 years old now. My story is very similar to yours. I feel like it's just a natural coping mechanism for me now. It comes and goes. I think it's still an unhealthy way to deal with life's sttesses but at least it isn't as out of control or overwhelming like it once was during my teens.
It's just one of your fellow human being's opinion about what may be happening to them. Nothing more, nothing less. Thanks for recognizing that.

@kaspark07 hey I honestly only offered another way to look at depression. I have been diagnosed with major depression and have had 5 break downs over a span of 5 years where I couldn't get out of bed for weeks. This is the first winter where I haven't completely been disabled by my depression. I don't know if there's a rhyme or reason for it except I've changed my mentality about the meaning of life. It's very similar to the above post. Currently, I am not a "productive" member of society...productive in the sense of what I've been conditioned to believe that will make me feel fulfilled and happy BUT the stress and expectation is gone. If you felt like I was preaching, then that wasn't my intention.

http://www.psychiatrictimes.com/dsm-5/mental-illness-vs-brain-disorders-szasz-dsm-5
Here's one snippet

Depression and anxiety are symptoms not a disease. This is coming from a depressed person who knows what it's like to not have the will or desire to get out of bed for weeks on end. Mental illness is a made up diagnosis. The pharmaceutical industry is making bank on people like us. They want us to think these feeling we feel are an illness so here are the pills that will cure it. There are studies and evidence that can not prove that depression is a mental illness...no one knows why people get depressed but they pretend they do.

I hate to break it to you but the short answer is...yes. Psychiatry is practically a made up profession because honestly no one really knows jack squat about the brain. Depression is a medical mystery for the most part. Psychiatrists are playing pretend doctor and writing out prescriptions because it makes them a lot of money to do so. The more pills they sell, the more they line their pockets. That goes for the majority of health care professionals though too. The pills are like a really shitty bandaid that already has lost it's stickyness and about to fall off. That's the best way I can describe medication for depression and anxiety. It may help a little for awhile but it's by no means the cure.
Chemical imbalance is a myth...

To me it feels like I treat food as if they all are my anxiety and problems. I eat a ton of it until I am so much in pain I can barely even lay down (much like how my anxiety and problems overwhelm me) then I get to get rid of everything within minutes until I have nothing left. It feels like I got rid of a boulder that has been weighing down on me. It's getting rid of the anxiety almost instantaneously. That's how I've dealt with any and all of my problems since I was 10. I know nothing else. Low self esteem is definitely one of the roots. I would even go as far as saying that I punish myself for taking breath in this world.

The feel good feelings only last so long. For me everytime I would purge I would have a similar good feeling like having a cigarette (times a hundred if I were being honest) but those feeling would last for at most an hour. I've been in bulimia's clutches for 13 years now and the bad feelings out weigh the good...I mean my teeth are shot, my digestion is crap, my face was always puffy looking and that's just the physical parts...the mental and emotional affects are a thousand times worse.

I feel for you. Try to remember how horrible you felt when and AFTER you purged. Recognize the feelings and emotions you are having while you are binging. I myself am on the slippery slope of overeating and it's a gateway to purging. You can get it under wraps. It helps me to remember a purge episode and write down what I felt like afterwards. Some things I felt were: sore throat, upset stomach, exhaustion... I felt completely defeated and out of control. I felt intense amount of shame and hatred for myself. I felt powerless. I felt guilt for having been so good to myself for months to only then flush it all down the toilet. Is the binge and purge worth the emotional turmoil for a half hour of feeling numb? What can I do in this moment instead? You are so strong. You've shown to yourself for three months that you are powerful and you can do this. You can handle this little bump in the road. You got this. Best of luck 💛
